skill.name: devflow
skill.description: Guides coordinated multi-agent development from issue assessment through PR review, human approval, and merge readiness checks.
skill.summary: Run a structured multi-agent development workflow with issue coverage gates, PR review, and merge checks.
skill.author: Cygnusfear

content.value_statement: Coordinated agent work can miss issue requirements or merge incomplete PRs. Devflow provides gates for task extraction, review, approval, and issue-linked merges.
actual_capabilities: Defines a five-phase workflow from assessment to merge.
Requires full issue requirement extraction before implementation.
Guides parallel agent dispatch with branch and PR rules.
Specifies a six-pass review process after CI passes.
Adds final coverage and issue-link checks before merge.
Recommends Mermaid diagrams for flows, states, and architecture changes.
limitations: Provides process guidance only and does not execute commands.
Assumes GitHub issues, pull requests, and GitHub CLI usage.
Uses Rust formatting as an example, so other stacks need adaptation.
Does not define Docker agent setup or access controls.

use_cases.title: Split a Large Issue
use_cases.description: Break one issue into parallel workstreams while preserving every requirement.

use_cases.title: Review Agent Pull Requests
use_cases.description: Check CI, requirement coverage, implementation quality, and issue links before merge.

use_cases.title: Manage Merge Readiness
use_cases.description: Confirm final coverage, human approval, and dependency order before merging PRs.

prompt_templates.title: Start an Issue Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Use devflow to assess issue #123 and list every requirement before planning implementation work.

prompt_templates.title: Dispatch Parallel Work
prompt_templates.prompt: Use devflow to split issue #123 into independent agent tasks with complete requirement coverage for each task.

prompt_templates.title: Run Review Gate
prompt_templates.scenario: Evaluate a pull request after CI passes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use devflow to review PR #456 against issue #123, including coverage, CI, code quality, and issue links.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Merge Decision
prompt_templates.scenario: Coordinate final approval and merge order.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use devflow to create a final merge readiness assessment for related PRs, including coverage evidence and dependency order.

output_examples.input: Assess issue #123 before assigning agent work.
output: Requirement list extracted from the issue.
Parallel task breakdown with ownership boundaries.
Dependencies and risks that need coordinator review.
Coverage table showing implemented, partial, and missing requirements.
Six-pass review notes for runtime, patterns, abstractions, environment, verification, and context.
Merge recommendation with required follow-up work.

output_examples.input: Prepare final merge readiness for multiple PRs.
output: Human approval status and unresolved decisions.
Recommended merge order based on dependencies.

best_practices: Extract all issue requirements before assigning implementation work.
Wait for CI before running the full review sequence.
Use evidence from files, tests, and PR metadata for coverage decisions.
anti_patterns: Merging a PR before every original requirement is verified.
Creating PRs without issue closure links or related issue notes.
Using diagrams as a substitute for concrete review evidence.

faq.question: Does this skill execute GitHub CLI commands?
faq.answer: No. It provides command examples and workflow steps that a user or agent may run manually.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: Is this only for Rust projects?
faq.answer: No. The workflow is general, but one formatting example uses cargo and should be adapted for other stacks.

faq.question: When should human approval happen?
faq.answer: Human approval is required for PR approval and complex decisions that need judgment.

faq.question: What makes a PR ready to merge?
faq.answer: A PR is ready when coverage is complete, CI passes, issue links exist, and required approvals are complete.

faq.question: Why does the skill mention Mermaid diagrams?
faq.answer: It recommends diagrams when changes involve flows, states, APIs, or architecture.
